thread:
Carla: Heads-up — ran into confusing microcopy in the tenant isolation section of the Dedicated runbook. "reserve" vs "preempt" are used interchangeably and that will trip up customers migrating policies.
Aisha: Oof, that's been a recurring note in the SDK docs too. Do you have a pointer?
Carla: Yep PR with fixes here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3456 — I left inline comments and a small YAML example, but the python snippet is still the old param name.
Ben: pinging to review, I noticed the python -> typescript parity is broken. The TS example uses "scale_policy: unified" while Python still references "legacy_scale".
Kevin: That's the root cause for a support ticket earlier this week. Should add a migration note (old -> unified) and a short deprecation banner.
Carla: Agreed. Proposal: replace ambiguous words with concrete definitions at top of section, add a migration table, and include two SDK snippets (py/ts) that match the yaml. Short and copyable.
Aisha: I can take the microcopy and the migration table. @Ben can you sync the SDK snippets to the runtime API so we don't ship wrong params?
Ben: Will do. Quick check — current recommended YAML (my suggestion):
```yaml
scale_policy:
  kind: unified_scalepolicy
  min_replicas: 1
  max_replicas: 10
  eviction_policy: preemptive
```
Ben: And python snippet should be:
```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient()
client.create_capacity("tenant-a", scale_policy={"kind":"unified_scalepolicy","min_replicas":1,"max_replicas":10,"eviction_policy":"preemptive"})
```
Carla: Perfect. Can you also add the small note explaining that "preemptive" means best-effort eviction vs reserved capacity? One sentence.
Ben: Yup, I'll add.
DocsBot: Created branch docs/clarify-isolation-1705 and opened PR #3456 for review — https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3456 :robot_face:
Aisha: I'll edit the intro paragraph: define reserve vs preempt, add short examples of customer impact (latency spike vs queued requests), and add the migration table with command-line examples.
Kevin: For the migration table can we add a one-liner CLI to convert old policies? e.g., `rictl migrate-scale --from legacy_scale --to unified_scalepolicy --tenant TENANT_ID` — we should mark this as a helper that uses the migration tool, not an authoritative API.
Carla: Good call. Add a "note: preview tool" badge. Also, small link fix: the runbook currently points to an internal design doc that moved. Update link to https://docs.redwood.ai/dedicated/scale-policy-design (I left the replacement in the PR description).
Aisha: I'll sweep the rest of the section for other broken links while making the microcopy edits.
Ben: After I update SDK snippets I'll run the doc build and smoke-check the code blocks: `make site && python -m http.server -d _site/ 8000` — will report back with any rendering issues.
Carla: Thanks. Can we aim to merge by EOD tomorrow? Support flagged this as medium priority.
Kevin: EOD sounds good. I'll queue a brief canary announce once merged so oncall knows expected behavior changes.
Aisha: Adding a small test prompt set to the PR so Optimize alerts don't fire after deploy — quick eval to ensure behavior parity.
Ben: Updated the PR with fixed snippets and link replacement. Also added a one-line changelog entry.
DocsBot: PR #3456 — reviewers requested: @Aisha, @Kevin. Status: ready for review.
Carla: Reviewing now, will leave minor nit comments and then approve. :thumbsup:
Aisha: Got it, will patch the wording and merge once approved.
Kevin: Thanks everyone — this should reduce a bunch of outbound confusion for tenants migrating to unified scalepolicy.
Carla: Closing loop: after merge we'll backport the migration note to the handbook landing page.
Ben: Noted — I'll open a follow-on PR for the handbook backport if needed.
DocsBot: Merge complete. PR #3456 merged into main at 1705000120.
